articles.title: Bihar Shock: Two Daughters Perform Mother’s Last Rites Alone After Village Turns Away
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Chhapra (Bihar): A deeply distressing incident from Jawainian village near Madhora, around 22 km from Chhapra, has triggered widespread outrage.

body.html:
Chhapra (Bihar): A deeply distressing incident from Jawainian village near Madhora, around 22 km from Chhapra, has triggered widespread outrage. Two young sisters were forced to carry their mother’s body and perform her last rites on their own after no one from the village came forward to help.

Babita Devi passed away a few days ago. Her husband, Ravindra Singh, had died about one-and-a-half years earlier, leaving the family in extreme poverty. Since then, the family had reportedly been living in isolation, struggling without social or financial support.

After Babita Devi’s death, villagers allegedly did not assist with funeral arrangements. With no relatives or neighbours stepping in, the two daughters gathered courage, carried their mother’s body, arranged the funeral pyre and performed the cremation rituals themselves.
The hardship continues even after the funeral. With no money, the sisters are now going door-to-door seeking help to perform the thirteenth-day Shraddha rituals. Locals claim prolonged poverty led to the family’s social neglect.

Activists and residents have urged the district administration to provide immediate financial aid, food support and long-term rehabilitation for the orphaned girls. The incident has gone viral on social media, with many calling it a grim reminder of growing social insensitivity and demanding government intervention.

articles.title: UP Shocker: Wife Seeks Divorce Just a Month After Marriage, Cites Husband’s Complexion
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Hathras (Uttar Pradesh): In a startling case from Hathras, a newlywed woman has sought divorce barely a month after her marriage, citing dissatisfaction with her husband’s appearance and marital relationship.

body.html:
Hathras (Uttar Pradesh): In a startling case from Hathras, a newlywed woman has sought divorce barely a month after her marriage, citing dissatisfaction with her husband’s appearance and marital relationship.

The couple—Abhishek Sharma (also referred to as Abhishek Saxena), a resident of Hathras, and Megha from Agra—had married with the consent of both families. However, within days of the wedding, differences reportedly surfaced, and the relationship began to deteriorate.

According to police sources, Megha told authorities that she was unhappy with her husband and did not wish to continue the marriage. She reportedly stated that she was dissatisfied with the physical relationship and had issues she did not want to discuss publicly. “I don’t want to live with him anymore and want to settle the matter at the police station,” she said.

Abhishek alleged that his wife objected to his dark complexion and had made up her mind to leave despite repeated efforts to reconcile. He said around ₹2.5–3 lakh was spent on the wedding and expressed deep distress over the sudden breakdown of the marriage.

Family members from both sides attempted mediation, and a local panchayat was also convened, but no compromise could be reached. Megha remained firm on her decision, and the couple separated within a month of marriage.

The case has sparked debate on social media, with users questioning whether marriages are increasingly being judged on physical appearance and expectations rather than compatibility and commitment.

articles.title: Fake Passport Racket Exposed in Ghaziabad: 24 Passports Issued on Bogus Addresses, 5 Arrested
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Ghaziabad (UP): Police in Ghaziabad have busted a gang involved in preparing fake passports using forged documents and bogus addresses.

body.html:
Ghaziabad (UP): Police in Ghaziabad have busted a gang involved in preparing fake passports using forged documents and bogus addresses. A case has been registered against 25 people in connection with the racket, in which 24 passports were issued and even delivered before the fraud came to light. Five accused have been arrested so far.

According to police, all 24 passports were prepared using fake addresses and forged documents, with the same mobile number used in every application. The fraud surfaced after officials of the Passport Department grew suspicious and sought a police probe.

Police said 24 passport applications were submitted from villages under the Bhojpur police station area, including Tyodi (12), Bhojpur (7), Saidpur Hussain (3), Kalchina (1) and Atrauli (1). On verification, police found that none of the applicants lived at the addresses mentioned, nor had they ever resided there.

The Regional Passport Officer (Delhi) wrote to the police on December 11, seeking investigation into the suspicious applications. During the probe, it was found that fake Aadhaar cards and other forged documents were used to obtain the passports.

Investigators further revealed that after the passports were prepared, two accused—Vivek Gandhi and Prakash Subba—approached postman Arun Kumar and informed him about the dispatch of the passports. He was instructed to call the applicants and hand over the passports directly instead of delivering them to the given addresses. The postman allegedly received ₹2,000 per passport for this.

Based on the investigation, Bhojpur police re-registered the case on Sunday and arrested five accused, including Vivek Gandhi, Prakash Subba, postman Arun Kumar, Amandeep Singh and Satwant Kaur. Fake documents were recovered from their possession.

Police sources said the possible involvement of police and intelligence officials in the verification process cannot be ruled out, though authorities have so far remained silent on the issue. Further investigation is underway.

articles.title: Female Lawyer, Family Assaulted by Toll Workers in Sonbhadra; Video Sparks Outrage, Probe On
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Sonbhadra (UP): A female lawyer and her family were allegedly assaulted by toll workers at the Lodhi (Markundi) toll plaza in Sonbhadra on Sunday (01 Feb 2026) afternoon, triggering widespread anger among the legal fraternity.

body.html:
Sonbhadra (UP): A female lawyer and her family were allegedly assaulted by toll workers at the Lodhi (Markundi) toll plaza in Sonbhadra on Sunday (01 Feb 2026) afternoon, triggering widespread anger among the legal fraternity. The incident falls under the jurisdiction of the Robertsganj police station.

According to reports, advocate Aarti Pandey was travelling from Obra to Robertsganj with her family around 3.30 pm when an argument broke out with toll staff over the toll fee and alleged delays at the plaza. The dispute soon escalated, with toll workers allegedly abusing and assaulting her family with sticks.

The lawyer alleged that when she tried to intervene, she was subjected to indecent behaviour and death threats. Three of her companions were injured in the incident and were rushed to the District Medical College. The condition of one injured woman is reported to be critical.

A passerby recorded the incident, and the video has since gone viral on social media, drawing sharp condemnation from lawyers. Following the incident, lawyers staged protests and demanded strict action against the accused toll workers.

On receiving information, police reached the spot and initiated an investigation. Officials said a case will be registered based on the complaint and legal action will follow. The Bar Association president also visited the medical college to meet the injured.

articles.title: MG Hector ‘Romeos’ Chase Family on Noida Roads, Obscene Gestures Caught on Camera; 2 Arrested
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Noida: A shocking case of road indiscipline and harassment has surfaced from Noida, where two youths allegedly chased a family’s car and made obscene gestures, including blowing flying kisses, in broad daylight.

body.html:
Noida: A shocking case of road indiscipline and harassment has surfaced from Noida, where two youths allegedly chased a family’s car and made obscene gestures, including blowing flying kisses, in broad daylight. The incident, captured on video, triggered widespread outrage after it went viral on social media.

According to the viral clip, the accused were travelling in an MG Hector and repeatedly followed a car carrying a family. They were seen making lewd gestures on a public road, leaving the occupants distressed and raising serious concerns over women’s and family safety even inside vehicles.

Social media users slammed the incident, questioning law and order in the high-tech city of Noida. Many alleged that such brazen behaviour reflected fearlessness among privileged youths, who appeared undeterred by police or social norms. Several users pointed out that the vehicle number was visible in the video and urged immediate police action.

Responding to the outrage, police said a case was registered and two accused — Amit Kumar from Azamgarh and Abhishek from Mainpuri, both currently residing in Noida — were arrested. The car used in the incident has been seized. Police added that the accused had also made obscene gestures at other women on the road and chased their vehicles.

Officials said further legal action is underway. The incident has reignited debate over road safety and women’s security in Uttar Pradesh, with citizens demanding strict punishment to ensure public roads are not turned into spaces for harassment.

articles.title: ‘My Name Is Mohammed Deepak’: Kotdwar Shop Row Sparks Debate on Identity and Communal Harmony
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Kotdwar: Tension flared in Kotdwar on January 28, 2026, after members of a right-wing organisation objected to the name of a shop run by a Muslim family, triggering a confrontation that has since gone viral on social media.

body.html:
Kotdwar: Tension flared in Kotdwar on January 28, 2026, after members of a right-wing organisation objected to the name of a shop run by a Muslim family, triggering a confrontation that has since gone viral on social media.

The incident occurred at Baba School Dress and Matching Centre on Patel Marg, a shop run for over 30 years by Wakeel Ahmed and his son Shoaib. A group of activists from the Bajrang Dal reportedly reached the shop and demanded that the word “Baba” be removed from its name, arguing that a Muslim-owned establishment should not use a term associated with Hindu saints.

During the confrontation, Deepak Kumar, a local gym trainer, intervened in support of the elderly shopkeeper. He questioned the group’s authority to dictate what name a business could use. When activists allegedly asked for his name and questioned why a Hindu was defending a Muslim, Deepak replied, “My name is Mohammed Deepak,” adding that humanity and citizenship matter more than religious identity. His response was captured on video and widely shared online.

Following the incident, activists from nearby areas, including Dehradun, reportedly staged protests against Deepak and his friend Vijay Rawat. As a precautionary measure amid rising tension, police briefly took Deepak to the Kotwali, citing his safety.

During the subsequent show of support, several local Muslim youths gathered in solidarity with Deepak. In a symbolic gesture highlighting communal harmony, Deepak and a Muslim youth were seen sharing water from the same bottle, an act that supporters said was meant to challenge social divisions based on religion.

Police later intervened to disperse the protesters and restore order in the town. Officials said the situation is under control and peace has been maintained.

The episode has sparked widespread discussion on social media, where Deepak has been praised by many for his stand against communal division. In a follow-up video message, he appealed for calm and harmony, urging people to “spread love, not hatred,” and said he considers himself a human being first.

#Kotdwar #UttarakhandNews #CommunalHarmony #IdeaOfIndia #ViralVideo #SocialMediaDebate #PeaceAndUnity #IndiaNews

articles.title: Selfie Madness on Highway: Couple Sits on Busy Road, Narrowly Escapes Death
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A disturbing video circulating widely on social media has sparked nationwide outrage after a couple was seen risking their lives by sitting in the middle of a busy highway to take a selfie.

body.html:
A disturbing video circulating widely on social media has sparked nationwide outrage after a couple was seen risking their lives by sitting in the middle of a busy highway to take a selfie. The incident could have ended in tragedy, as fast-moving vehicles were seen passing dangerously close to them.

In the viral footage, a speeding car is forced to brake abruptly to avoid hitting the couple, missing them by just inches. The near-collision shocked viewers, who noted that the situation could easily have resulted in a fatal accident. Instead of showing remorse, the couple allegedly confronted the driver, questioning why he could not see them on what they claimed was a “wide empty road,” despite clearly occupying an active traffic lane.

The video has drawn sharp criticism online, with users slamming the couple’s reckless behaviour and lack of civic sense. Many pointed out that such stunts, done for social media attention, put not only the individuals involved at risk but also endanger unsuspecting commuters.

Several users also highlighted that in the event of an accident, drivers are often unfairly blamed, even when pedestrians or selfie-seekers are clearly at fault.

The incident has once again raised concerns over the growing trend of dangerous photo and video shoots on highways, bridges and expressways across India. Authorities have repeatedly warned that stopping vehicles or sitting on high-speed roads for photography is illegal and can invite heavy fines, licence suspension and even jail under traffic safety laws.

Traffic officials and road safety experts reiterated that highways are meant strictly for fast-moving vehicles, not photography, and even a moment’s negligence can lead to irreversible loss of life.

articles.title: Drain Excavation Turns Disaster: Two Houses Collapse in Bhathat, Villagers Blame Negligence
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Bhathat: Two houses collapsed on Friday morning during drain excavation work in Badhariya Tola of Bhathat area, under Gulriha police station limits. No casualties were reported, as residents managed to escape in time, but household belongings were buried under the debris.

body.html:
Bhathat: Two houses collapsed on Friday morning during drain excavation work in Badhariya Tola of Bhathat area, under Gulriha police station limits. No casualties were reported, as residents managed to escape in time, but household belongings were buried under the debris.

According to residents, a machine was used to excavate a drain in Barharia Tola on Thursday night. By Friday morning, houses located along the bank of the excavation began to shake. Sensing danger, family members rushed out to save their lives. Within minutes, a three-storey, two-room house belonging to Kitabullah collapsed in just about ten seconds.

A nearby one-storey, two-room house owned by Nazrun, wife of Luqman, was also completely destroyed. Furniture, utensils, ration, clothes, water motor and other essential items were buried and damaged under the rubble. The affected families struggled for hours to retrieve whatever they could from the debris.

The families said the houses were built with their lifetime savings and were reduced to ruins in moments. Following the incident, a large number of villagers gathered at the site. On receiving information, Regional Lekhpal Rajat Verma and PWD Junior Engineer Umashankar Gupta reached the spot and assessed the damage.

Public Works Department officials assured the affected families of compensation. Meanwhile, villagers accused the contractor and machine operator of negligence, alleging that the drain was being excavated deeper than required and soil was being removed irresponsibly. Residents also claimed that another house in the same locality had been damaged earlier during similar excavation work.

#Bhathat #UPNews #HouseCollapse #PWDWork #Negligence #Gulriha #InfrastructureFailure #VillageNews #IndiaNews

articles.title: One Slip Away From Death: Pointsman Saves Passenger Under Moving Train at Prayagraj Station
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A pointsman’s quick reflexes saved a passenger’s life at Naini railway station in Prayagraj on Saturday evening around 4 pm.

body.html:
A pointsman’s quick reflexes saved a passenger’s life at Naini railway station in Prayagraj on Saturday evening around 4 pm. The incident occurred at platform number four when a passenger attempted to board the moving 11071 Kamayani Express and slipped, falling into the gap between the train and the platform.

Pointsman Sube Singh Chaudhary, who was on duty, immediately rushed in and pulled the passenger to safety. A crowd soon gathered at the platform after the dramatic rescue.

Sube Singh, originally from the Bikaner division, is currently posted at Naini station under the Prayagraj division for special duty during the Magh Mela.

Divisional Railway Manager Rajneesh Agrawal praised his bravery, stating that the act brought pride to the Prayagraj division. He also urged passengers not to board or alight from moving trains and to do so only after trains come to a complete halt to prevent such incidents.

articles.title: Man Accused of Hiding Identity, Forcing Conversion; ‘Love Jihad’ FIR Filed, Accused Counters Claims
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Aligarh: A controversial case has emerged from Aligarh district of Uttar Pradesh, where a woman has accused a man of hiding his identity, trapping her in a relationship, forcibly converting her to Islam and later abandoning her.

body.html:
Aligarh: A controversial case has emerged from Aligarh district of Uttar Pradesh, where a woman has accused a man of hiding his identity, trapping her in a relationship, forcibly converting her to Islam and later abandoning her. The matter came to light after the woman approached the police seeking justice, following which an FIR was registered on serious charges.

According to the complaint, the victim, a resident of Rorawar, alleged that a man named Firoz contacted her using the name “Rakesh.” She claimed he lured her with the promise of a job, drugged her by mixing a substance in her cold drink, and sexually assaulted her. She further alleged that the act was recorded and later used to blackmail her. The woman said she was pressured into converting to Islam, her name was changed to Alia, and she was married to Firoz. She alleged that she was later abandoned and threatened with death when she protested.

The victim, who now has a young child, approached the SSP’s office demanding strict action. Police have registered a case against Firoz under charges including fraud, r@pe, blackmail and criminal intimidation. The woman has also alleged forced religious conversion.

After the FIR was filed, Firoz released a video presenting his version of events. In the video, he claimed to be a resident of Tarasur Khurd and said he works in a factory where he met the woman around two to two-and-a-half years ago. He denied the allegations and claimed their relationship developed mutually.

Firoz alleged that the documents being circulated by the woman were fake and demanded a thorough investigation. He said a Nikah certificate always bears a mosque seal and is recorded in a register, which he claimed could be verified. He also alleged that he had spent ₹6–7 lakh on the woman, was constructing a house for her, had given her a plot of land, and transferred money to her bank account, claiming to have proof.

He further alleged that the woman was demanding ₹5 lakh from him and that after he refused, she approached the media and police. Calling the allegations false, Firoz requested the authorities to investigate the case impartially.

Police said the matter is under investigation and all allegations and counter-claims will be examined based on evidence.
